goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of five uncurated IMA-approved single-reference critical-element mineral species from the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 32, 36, 37, and 38): zhiqinite (IMA:2019-077), belmonteite (IMA:2024-040), dacostaite (IMA:2024-015), fluormacraeite (IMA:2024-054), and macraeite (IMA:2023-065). Reclassified bonacinaite (IMA:2018-056) to the multi-reference queue because the IMA Master List cites two references (Mineralogical Magazine 84 (2020), 568 and European Journal of Mineralogy 36 (2024), 863).

curated_sources_and_records.name: Zhiqinite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Inclusion in a corundum grain (>200 um) separated from podiform chromitite orebody Cr-11, Luobusa ophiolite, Yarlung Zangbo suture zone, ~200 km ESE of Lhasa, Tibet, China
type_specimens: Holotype M13817 (source of focused-ion-beam TEM foil no. 5358) and FIB foil no. 5358, deposited at the Chinese Geological Museum, Xisiyangrouhutong 15th, Xicheng District, Beijing, China

primary_source.citation: Xiong F, Xu X, Mugnaioli E, Gemmi M, Wirth R, Grew ES, Robinson PT, Yang J (2020) Two new minerals, badengzhuite, TiP, and zhiqinite, TiSi2, from the Cr-11 chromitite orebody, Luobusa ophiolite, Tibet, China: is this evidence for super-reduced mantle-derived fluids? European Journal of Mineralogy 32:557-574

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 3 (p. 564) standardless TEM-EDX chemistry (n = 4 analyses at points 428, 429, 430, and 431 in foil no. 5358: mean Si 57.61 wt% [SD 2.15, range 55.21-60.42 wt%; 69.84 at.%, SD 1.85], Ti 42.39 wt% [SD 2.15, range 39.58-44.79 wt%; 30.16 at.%, SD 1.85], sum 100 wt%, empirical formula Ti0.905Si2.095 on the basis of 3 cations/atoms)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 557) describes zhiqinite as having 'a primitive orthorhombic cell' with space group Fddd, whereas Section 5.4 and Figure 6 (p. 566) confirm that space group Fddd (#70) has an F-centered orthorhombic lattice with characteristic chess-board extinctions and hk0: h + k = 4n d-glide conditions.

Section 4.1 (pp. 560-563) and Section 6.2 (pp. 568-569) document the scientific controversy raised by Litasov et al. (2019a,b) alleging that the Cr-11 corundum grains and enclosed ultra-reduced phases represent anthropogenic brown fused alumina abrasive, which Xiong et al. (2020) rebut on the basis of mineralogical and textural differences.

primary_source.citation: Biagioni C, Sejkora J, Dolnicek Z (2026) Belmonteite, CaMn2(AsO4)2(H2O)5*2H2O, a new arsenate mineral from the Mn ore deposits of the Graveglia Valley, eastern Liguria, Italy. European Journal of Mineralogy 38:531-543

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 534) EPMA chemistry (n = 8 spot analyses: As2O5 48.57, MnO 29.94, CaO 10.12, CuO 1.28, Al2O3 0.22, K2O 0.10, H2Ocalc 26.51, unnormalized total 116.74 wt%, normalized total 100.00 wt%, empirical formula (Ca0.86Mn0.11K0.01)Sigma0.98(Mn1.90Cu0.08Al0.02)Sigma2.00As2.01O8*7H2O on the basis of 15 O apfu)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 4 (p. 533) reports the ideal oxide composition for stoichiometric CaMn2(AsO4)2*7H2O as As2O5 41.49, CaO 10.12, MnO 25.61, and H2O 22.77 wt% for a printed sum of 100.00 wt%, whereas the four rounded constituent values sum to 99.99 wt%.

Table 2 (p. 537) prints both calculated d-spacing column headers as 'd*calc' instead of 'd*calc' and 'dcalc' and misprints d*calc = 2.224 A for reflection (0 4 5) alongside dobs = 2.446 A and dcalc = 2.449 A (where the true powder-cell spacing is 2.450 A).

type_specimens: Holotype 20073 (Museo di Storia Naturale, University of Pisa, Via Roma 79, Calci, Pisa, Italy)

primary_source.citation: Biagioni C, Mauro D, Sejkora J, Dolnicek Z, Dini A, Skoda R (2025) Dacostaite, K(Mg2Al)[Mg(H2O)6]2(AsO4)2F6 * 2H2O, a new fluoride-arsenate mineral from the Cetine di Cotorniano Mine (Tuscany, Italy). European Journal of Mineralogy 37:39-52

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 42) EPMA chemistry (n = 10 spot analyses: As2O5 35.42, MgO 21.13, F 13.15, Al2O3 12.23, K2O 4.13, CuO 0.42, CaO 0.36, ZnO 0.34, P2O5 0.17, Na2O 0.15, MnO 0.04, FeO 0.04, sum 87.58, O=-F -5.54, H2Ocalc 41.40, unnormalized total 123.44 wt%, normalized total 100.00 wt%, empirical formula (K0.56Ca0.04Na0.03[]0.37)Sigma1.00(Al1.54Mg1.38Cu0.03Zn0.03)Sigma2.98[Mg(H2O)6]2[(As0.99P0.01)O4]2[F4.46(OH)1.46O0.08]Sigma6.00*2H2O)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Table 3 (p. 43) prints the h index range as '-15 <=h15' with a missing '<=' symbol.
Section 4.3.2 (pp. 43 and 45) cites bond-valence sums of 5.14 v.u. for As(1) and 2.52 and 2.53 v.u. for M(1) and M(2), whereas Table 6 (p. 45) lists 5.11, 2.54, and 2.54 v.u., respectively.

Section 4.3.3 (p. 46) states that 'O(2) accepts H bonds from two Ow(2) groups', whereas Tables 6 and 7 show that O(2) accepts two H bonds from Ow(3) at 2.670(13) A while Ow(2) donates H bonds to O(1) at 2.763(10) A.

European Journal of Mineralogy 37:169-179

curated_sources_and_records.chemistry_summary: Table 1 (p. 171) cold-stage EPMA chemistry (n = 8 analyses on 2 crystals: P2O5 28.51, Fe2O3 14.74, MnO 12.49, TiO2 8.19, K2O 4.41, F 1.55, MgO 1.07, Al2O3 0.65, H2Ocalc 27.13, -O=F -0.65, printed Total 98.10 wt%, exact arithmetic sum 98.09 wt%, structural empirical formula A1[K0.14(H2O)0.76]Sigma0.90A2[K0.79(H2O)0.21]Sigma1.00M1(Mn2+1.75Mg0.25)Sigma2.00M2+M3(Fe3+1.84Al0.13Ti4+1.02Mg0.01)Sigma3.00(PO4)4.00X[O0.94F0.81(OH)0.25]Sigma2.00(H2O)10*3.90H2O)
primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 1 (p. 170) reports the Plossberg locality as 18 km from Hagendorf, whereas Section 2 (p. 170) states 15 km north-northeast of Hagendorf.

Table 1 (p. 171) prints Total = 98.10 wt%, whereas the exact arithmetic sum of the printed mean constituents (P2O5 28.51 + Fe2O3 14.74 + MnO 12.49 + TiO2 8.19 + K2O 4.41 + F 1.55 + MgO 1.07 + Al2O3 0.65 + H2Ocalc 27.13 - O=F 0.65) is 98.09 wt%.
The Abstract (p. 169) mislabels Robs = 0.0559 as 'wRobs = 0.0559' for 5646 reflections with I > 3sigma(I), whereas Table 3 (p. 173) and Section 6.2 confirm Robs = 0.0559 and wRobs = 0.0700.

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Table 7 (p. 277) misprints the ideal formula of macraeite as '[(H2O)K]Mn2(Fe2Ti)(PO4)4[(O(OH)]2(H2O)10*4H2O'.
Section 5 (p. 270) prints 3460 cm-1 twice in the list of O-H stretching shoulder wavenumbers ('shoulders at 3580, 3460 and 3250 cm-1' on the band centred at 3460 cm-1).

The Abstract (p. 267), Section 6.2 (pp. 270 and 272), and Table 3 (p. 273) exhibit minor internal differences in wRobs (0.065 vs 0.063), synchrotron wavelength (0.7109 vs 0.7107 A), and observed reflection count (4979 vs 4990).
